title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to ensure that all AI systems used within the state are fully disclosed, with clear information on how they operate and the data they use. It establishes requirements for regular reporting and accountability measures to protect citizens from opaque AI practices.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in handling veterans' claims, ensuring that any automated decision‑making processes are transparent, fair, and subject to oversight. The act would establish guidelines for developing, testing, and monitoring AI systems to protect veterans’ rights and improve the accuracy and reliability of claim decisions.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law designed to protect the integrity of elections from misinformation created by artificial intelligence. It establishes rules, oversight, and penalties to prevent AI‑generated deception from influencing voters and to promote transparency in how AI is used during electoral processes.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes a framework for funding and regulating AI research to prioritize reliability, safety, and accountability. It requires developers to conduct thorough testing, disclose risks, and report to an oversight body that ensures AI systems meet strict reliability standards.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard people from misleading AI practices by requiring that AI systems be clearly labeled and that their outputs be transparent and honest. It sets rules for how companies must disclose AI usage and imposes penalties for deceptive or deceptive AI marketing.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act requires AI developers to build strong security measures into their systems and to carry out regular risk assessments. It also sets up a regulatory framework for ongoing monitoring, transparency, and protection against cyber threats in AI technologies.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to oversee the security of artificial intelligence systems. It focuses on developing guidelines, coordinating with industry and government, and mitigating AI‑related cyber threats to protect national infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive guidelines for identifying, assessing, and mitigating the risks associated with the development, deployment, and operation of artificial intelligence systems. It also mandates transparency, accountability, and robust protective measures to safeguard data, privacy, and public safety in the use of AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at establishing a national framework for the safe development, deployment, and oversight of physical AI technologies, such as autonomous robots and machines that interact with the physical world. The act seeks to coordinate federal agencies, set industry standards, and create regulatory oversight to ensure these systems operate responsibly and protect public safety.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The policy amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require that any political advertisement containing AI‑generated images or video must include a disclosure statement within the ad itself. This change is intended to increase transparency and accountability regarding the use of generative AI in campaign communications.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to prevent artificial intelligence from spreading misleading or manipulative content that could influence the outcome of elections. It requires that any AI-generated political content be clearly labeled, restricts the use of AI for targeted political persuasion, and establishes penalties for violations to safeguard the integrity of the democratic process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes legal requirements for overseeing AI systems that can modify their own behavior. It mandates transparency, accountability, and periodic audits to ensure these systems operate safely and ethically.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent artificial intelligence systems from operating in ways that could pose serious safety or security threats. It calls for stricter oversight, accountability standards, and potential restrictions on AI technologies that are deemed too dangerous or unpredictable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or expanding data centers that support AI development, allowing time to evaluate their impact. This measure aims to assess environmental, energy, and societal effects before proceeding with large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board tasked with investigating and addressing security risks posed by artificial intelligence systems. It provides the board with authority to conduct audits, enforce regulations, and coordinate with industry and law‑enforcement agencies to safeguard national cybersecurity.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposed law that aims to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence so that it benefits the American people. It focuses on encouraging responsible innovation, protecting jobs, and ensuring that AI technologies are fair, safe, and contribute to the country’s economic and national security.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI companies operating in China to submit regular reports on how much energy their AI systems use and what environmental impact they have. This law aims to monitor, regulate, and reduce the carbon footprint associated with AI development and deployment across the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that bars artificial intelligence from diagnosing, treating, or prescribing medical care without a licensed human doctor’s oversight. It is designed to protect patients by ensuring all medical decisions are made by qualified doctors and imposes penalties on any AI system that tries to replace a human physician.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The proposal aims to create a new office under the President’s Executive Office that focuses on artificial intelligence and emerging technology threats. This office would monitor, assess, and coordinate responses to risks from AI and other advanced technologies across the federal government.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI-related issues. The committee will study AI policy, recommend best practices, and advise lawmakers on the nation’s AI strategy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a national framework for assessing the risks of AI systems, mandating thorough risk evaluations before deployment. It requires developers, users, and regulators to identify potential harms, implement mitigation strategies, and comply with oversight to ensure AI technologies are safe and accountable.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a legislative framework aimed at regulating artificial intelligence technologies. It seeks to establish standards for safety, transparency, and accountability while fostering innovation and protecting citizens' rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 requires companies that develop or run AI systems to evaluate and reduce their environmental footprints, including energy use and carbon emissions. It sets up reporting obligations, offers incentives for greener practices, and imposes penalties for non‑compliance to encourage the development of more sustainable AI technologies.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: This act establishes a national framework to integrate AI literacy into K‑12 education, requiring schools to provide teachers with training and students with curriculum that teaches the basics of AI, its impacts, and safe use. It also sets standards for equitable access to AI resources and ensures that all students are prepared for a future where AI technologies are integral to daily life.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a law designed to ensure that AI systems are developed and tested with rigorous reliability standards. It establishes government oversight, testing protocols, and accountability measures so that AI technologies are safe, transparent, and trustworthy before they reach the public.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also outlines steps for implementation, evaluation, and coordination with other agencies to strengthen national cyber defense.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law that calls for AI education to be built into K‑12 schools, so students learn how AI works and how to think critically about it. The act would give schools guidelines, resources and standards to help students develop basic AI skills and become ready for an AI‑driven world.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act establishes a national program to educate the public about AI, its benefits, risks, and ethical considerations. It seeks to promote informed decision‑making and responsible use of AI technologies through public outreach, curriculum integration, and collaboration with stakeholders.
